rationale: Regression-checked git diff 8b3a5535 e7388f71 against the resulting spec and relevant lifecycle/panel primitives. The diff introduces no defect in the G2 trust-boundary lens. SHA value classes prevent hostile operands and keep placeholders non-corroborating; absent commit objects still refuse. The clarified checkout-local panel visibility and panel-edit residual accurately describe existing unauthenticated evidence. The typed plan-source probe explicitly distinguishes absence from failures. This approves the specification, not an implementation of its proposed behavior.

findings.title: Round-6 ask status
findings.detail: No G2 round-6 required changes or minor asks need confirmation. The prior G2 verdict approved and had an empty concrete_changes_required array. Its implementation caution about preserving raw panel scan errors remains covered by F5 and is not weakened by this diff.

findings.title: SHA classification does not add corroboration authority
findings.detail: R4.2 F2 classifies values before git calls, and R4.3 admits only well-formed object IDs into its corroborating set. Empty and placeholder values cannot confirm a primary-path candidate; option-like and revision-expression values refuse F2 without reaching git. A well-formed but locally absent commit refuses as UnlandedReview. Rewriting an outside-tip SHA to an empty value or placeholder can bypass F2, but requires the same panel-file write authority that already permits deleting the registration or replacing its SHA with a landed SHA. This stays within the expressly accepted panel-edit residual, rather than granting new authority to a bd-metadata-only forge. F1, F3, F4, tuple equality and read-time checks remain mandatory.

findings.title: Visibility and forge reach are stated accurately
findings.detail: The invoking-checkout limitation is now explicit and pinned by AC-11(x-w), including the differing result when untracked registrations are absent from another worktree. This does not change the previously checkout-local scan. Audit metadata and panel files remain agent-writable, and a git-history author can fabricate a source-naming merge subject; the spec does not elevate them to authenticated operator intent. The revised residual correctly distinguishes the existing forge mechanism from its new bounded off-first-parent reach. AC-11(vii-a) retains refusal after an unreviewed amend and offers a scoped override rather than panel deletion.

findings.title: Plan-source fallback remains fail-closed on errors
findings.detail: The new helper contract permits checkout fallback only for a missing branch or missing path. Non-zero ls-tree failures and other git errors refuse. AC-1 adds both an absent-blob fixture and a probe-failure fixture, preventing an infrastructure failure from silently changing the mapping source. No selection, evidence-file or scoped-override authority is widened elsewhere in the diff.

Two historical caveats remain: the older round-6 unqualified registration-count statement excludes non-spec panels (already corrected in the reviewed spec), and the generic git worktree add probe example would write administrative state into the read-only source repository.
